newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha eases on weaker crude, slack demand.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha eases on weaker crude, slack demand.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices fell in thin trade on Friday, weighed down by weaker European markets and an overnight loss in crude, traders said.
"It's mostly (lower) crude and (weaker) Europe, but end-user demand is not that good either," one trader said.
Offers for open-spec naphtha second-half September were heard at $199.00 per tonne, while bids were notionally assessed at $197.50.
In near-term naphtha spreads, the contango narrowed slightly, with second-half August/second-half September quoted at minus $2.00/minus $1.00.

Indonesia's low sulphur waxy residue (LSWR) allocation for July, which totalled 2.3 million barrels compared to 3.1 million for June, is expected to set a bullish tone not only in the fuel oil market but in low sulphur crude oil trading, traders said.

Tight availability for July will force regular buyers of Indonesian barrels to look to other sources of supply, such as Singapore cargoes, relatively expensive straight-run material from Malaysia and possibly low sulphur crude such as Indonesia's Minas and China's Daqing crude, they added.
